newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little moved, physical market quiet.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little moved, physical market quiet.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were barely changed on Wednesday as overnight overseas crude markets provided little market direction, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half July was quoted at $206.00/207.00 per tonne after it was sold by a European major to a European trader at $206.25 in early afternoon trading.
First-half July was notionally assessed at around $205.00/206.00.
In physical trading, petrochemical product manufacturers were in no hurry to procure supplies because of ample regional availability, traders said.
"No one is rushing to the market because there is a fair amount of prompt supplies in Asia now," one trader with petrochemical end-user said.

In middle distillates, one Japanese refiner bought about 20,000 kilolitres of jet fuel to be delivered to Chiba, near Tokyo, in the first half of June, at slightly higher than $1.30 over the mean of Singapore quotes per barrel, traders said.
The level of the deal is a little higher than the current market level because the cargo is smaller than the regular volume of 25,000 to 30,000 kilolitres, they said.
